In [[axiomatic set theory]], '''Shelah cardinals''' are a kind of [[large cardinal]]s. A [[cardinal number|cardinal]] <math>\kappa</math> is called Shelah [[iff]] for every <math>f:\kappa\rightarrow\kappa</math>, there exists a [[transitive class]] <math>N</math> and an [[elementary embedding]] <math>j:V\rightarrow N</math> with [[critical point (set theory)|critical point]] <math>\kappa</math>; and <math>V_{j(f)(\kappa )}\subset N</math>.

A Shelah cardinal has a normal [[Ultrafilter (set theory)|ultrafilter]] containing the set of [[weakly hyper-Woodin cardinal]]s below it.
